channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Judge rejects Trump policy allowing swift deportations to alternate countries
item.description: A Boston federal judge ruled the Trump administration's policy permitting swift deportations to countries other than migrants' origin is unlawful and must be struck down.

item.title: Contract – Chapter 93A – Causation
item.description: Where a plaintiff brought a G.L.c. 93A complaint against a defendant contractor that violated G.L.c. 142A by failing to provide a qualifying contract, a judgment for the defendant after a jury-waived trial should be affirmed because nothing in the record supports the plaintiff’s contention that the trial court was clearly erroneous in finding that the plaintiff failed to sustain his burden of establishing a causal connection between the violation and any alleged loss or injury.

item.title: Civil practice – Failure to appear
item.description: Where a plaintiff was awarded summary judgment after a hearing at which the defendant did not appear, the subsequent denial of the defendant’s motion to vacate that judgment should be upheld because the summary judgment ruling was made on the merits of the motion and was not premised upon the defendant’s failure to appear.

item.title: Real property – Reformation – Mutual mistake
item.description: Where a plaintiff has filed a complaint seeking reformation of a deed, a motion to dismiss the complaint should be denied because the plaintiff has stated a claim for reformation based on a scrivener’s error.

item.title: Retirement – Purchase of service
item.description: Where the State Board of Retirement denied a petitioner’s request to purchase creditable service, that decision must be reversed because the petitioner applied to buy back her 1988-2001 service before the date any retirement allowance became effective for her, so nothing stands in the way of her purchasing her 1998-2001 service and she is entitled to do so.

item.title: Licenses and permits – Day care
item.description: Where a petitioner has appealed from a determination of the Department of Early Education and Care that she is unsuitable to operate a day care program, that determination should be upheld because the petitioner has not presented clear and convincing evidence of her suitability to operate an early education and care program.

item.title: Workers’ compensation – Waiver – ‘Double recovery’
item.description: Where an administrative judge ordered an insurance company to pay benefits to an employee who was injured while working for an uninsured subcontractor, the order should be affirmed because the insurer waived any “double recovery” issue.

item.title: California judge dismisses xAI trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI
item.description: A California federal judge dismissed xAI's trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, citing lack of allegations against OpenAI itself. xAI may amend and refile by March 17.

item.title: Auditor pushes back on AG’s audit dispute intervention
item.description: State Auditor Diana DiZoglio requests Supreme Judicial Court approval to hire legal counsel to dispute Attorney General Andrea Campbell's intervention in her audit lawsuit.

item.title: SJC issues call for amicus briefs in posted cases
item.description: The SJC is seeking amicus briefs in several upcoming cases.
